stories.title: India Inc's CSR gap widens to a decade high
stories.summary: BSE 200 companies left a record 2,290 crore of CSR obligations unspent in FY26, up from 1,920 crore the previous year. With excess spending also falling, the net shortfall of 1,183 crore is the widest in over a decade. Corporate social responsibility is becoming less social.

stories.title: Few Pakistani firms commit to children's rights
stories.summary: Only 3 percent of 98 companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange explicitly disclose a commitment to children's rights. While 78 percent report community investments benefiting children, the findings from a new assessment suggest that explicit policy commitments remain a rarity in the local corporate sector.

stories.title: MCA proposes voluntary CSR impact assessments
stories.summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has released draft rules to make CSR impact assessments voluntary for all companies, regardless of their spending obligations. Current rules require firms with an average obligation of 10 crore or more to commission independent assessments. Oversight is being encouraged to take a break.

stories.title: MCA expands list of qualifying CSR activities
stories.summary: A draft revision of Schedule VII of the Companies Act adds mental health, telemedicine, and career counselling to the list of qualifying CSR activities. The update also includes the Prime Minister's Internship Scheme. The government is effectively broadening the definition of what counts as corporate social responsibility.

stories.title: MCA draft rules target one-off CSR spending
stories.summary: New draft rules from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs would prohibit companies from counting one-off events, government schemes, corpus funds, or free product distribution as CSR. The ministry is seeking to narrow the scope of acceptable spending. Stakeholders have until December 11 to provide their feedback.

stories.title: ISSB urged to make its nature-related disclosure a standard - ESG Dive
EU raises sustainability reporting thresholds
stories.summary: The EU's Omnibus I Directive has increased sustainability reporting thresholds to 1,000 employees and 450 million euros in turnover. This change pushes many non-EU groups out of scope until 2029. Regulatory relief is arriving for those who managed to stay just small enough.

stories.title: New grant for large businesses to defray costs of sustainability reporting - Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)

G77 alleges division and lack of transparency at COP31
stories.summary: Developing nations have accused developed countries of dividing the G77 bloc and hindering progress on a climate finance roadmap. As the UN conference runs past its scheduled close, the coalition of 134 countries and China continues to wait for a final outcome document that addresses their demands.

stories.title: COP31 climate finance talks remain deadlocked
stories.summary: Climate finance negotiations at COP31 are stalled as countries remain divided over financial support. Negotiators are currently waiting for a revised text from the conference presidency while delegations face uncertainty over the extended timeline. The plenary venue remains largely empty as discussions continue behind closed doors.

stories.title: UK and EU align on carbon border rules
stories.summary: The UK will exempt EU goods from its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism starting January 2027, one year before the EU reciprocates. To secure the deal, the UK has committed to aligning with EU free allocation rules. The two regions are coordinating their exits from carbon allowances.

EU recognizes Albanian, Montenegrin, Serbian carbon pricing within CBAM
stories.summary: The European Union has recognized carbon pricing schemes from 24 countries, including three in the Western Balkans to Albania, Montenegro, and Serbia. Among the non-EU countries covered by Balkan Green Energy News, Turkey is also on the list. The European Union’s decision opens the possibility that the CO2 tax paid

stories.title: UK and EU agree to link carbon markets
stories.summary: The UK and EU have reached an agreement to link their emissions trading systems by 2028. The package includes plans to reduce trade friction for food and drink and commits both sides to further talks regarding the UK re-joining the EU electricity market. Trading is becoming more collaborative.

stories.title: Climate summit enters overtime
stories.summary: The 31st UN climate summit in Turkey has extended beyond its scheduled conclusion as delegates struggle to reach a consensus. Presidency officials are currently drafting a final cover decision, with negotiators expected to reconvene after reviewing the text. The summit is officially still in session.

stories.title: Cop31 talks risk no deal as climate finance and fossil fuel disputes persist - Traders Union
COP31 talks stall over fossil fuel language
stories.summary: Negotiations at COP31 in Turkey remain deadlocked following a dispute over the inclusion of a fossil fuel phase-out in the final agreement. Proceedings were suspended Saturday night to allow for a new draft. The conference, originally scheduled to end Friday, remains without a resolution.

stories.title: Nations clash over fossil fuel transition
stories.summary: Climate talks in Turkey have stalled as a coalition of 130 countries pushes for a reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels in the final outcome. Co-conveners held meetings throughout Saturday to address the impasse, as frustration grows over the lack of progress after two weeks.

stories.title: COP31 deadlock continues
stories.summary: Negotiations at the UN climate summit in Turkey are suspended after running more than a day over time. Disagreements persist over fossil fuel demand and funding for climate adaptation. Negotiating teams are currently moving their departure plans as the deadlock remains unresolved.

stories.title: COP31 deadlock continues
stories.summary: Negotiations at the UN climate summit in Turkey are suspended after running more than a day over time. Disagreements persist over fossil fuel demand and funding for climate adaptation. Negotiating teams are currently moving their departure plans as the deadlock remains unresolved.

stories.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science - France 24
Climate summit venue packs up
stories.summary: Work crews have begun dismantling the venue for the United Nations climate talks in Turkey. The conference, which was scheduled to conclude on Friday, remains in overtime as nations continue to negotiate a response to global warming.

stories.title: COP31 negotiations extend into extra time
stories.summary: Negotiations at the UN climate summit in Turkey have entered extra time as consensus on the final document remains elusive. Deep divisions persist regarding fossil fuel emissions and the economic growth demands of the Global South. Negotiators worked through the night to address energy and finance.

stories.title: Taiwan eyes circular economy cooperation
stories.summary: Taiwan plans to collaborate with international partners on circular economy initiatives following the conclusion of COP31. Minister of Environment Peng Chi-ming stated the nation must improve resource efficiency, noting that Taiwan currently relies on imports for 76.14 percent of its raw materials.

stories.title: Indonesia and Netherlands sign waste agreement
stories.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of Environment and the Dutch government have signed a memorandum of understanding on waste management and circular economy cooperation for 2026 to 2030. The agreement was finalized on the sidelines of the COP31 summit in Turkey to support national greenhouse gas reduction efforts.

stories.title: Brazil reports circular economy value
stories.summary: A survey by Brazil’s National Confederation of Industry estimates the circular economy generates up to 15.8 billion USD annually. Presented at COP31, the study notes that funds allocated to circularity account for up to 10.3 percent of the country's sustainable finance market, exceeding the global average.

stories.title: Circular farming linked to economic performance
stories.summary: A study of Palestinian agricultural value chains indicates that adopting circular economy principles correlates with improved economic and environmental performance. Published in the Journal of the Saudi Society of Agricultural Sciences, the research suggests restructuring traditional linear models benefits rural farming operations.

stories.title: Councils suspend fridge collections
stories.summary: The Local Government Association is calling for urgent action to address a growing backlog of old fridges. Nearly a third of local councils have suspended collection services, citing an unacceptable strain on current resources.

stories.title: Supply chain emissions challenge green transport
stories.summary: Supply chain emissions for light-duty vehicles are projected to reach 60 to 70 percent of their total lifecycle footprint as electrification scales. While tailpipe emissions fall, the carbon footprint is migrating to the production of batteries, steel, and aluminum.

stories.title: Researchers defend academic critique of circularity
stories.summary: Researchers argue that academic critique is an essential developmental process for the circular economy rather than a threat. Writing in the Journal of Industrial Ecology, they contend that framing circularity as an embattled concept misidentifies the hazards facing sustainable transitions.

stories.title: EU bans plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries
stories.summary: The European Union has prohibited the export of plastic waste to non-OECD countries effective 21 November 2026. Under the new Waste Shipment Regulation, the EU aims to strengthen its internal circular economy and ensure that exported waste does not harm the environment or human health.

stories.title: Island nations call for packaging reform
stories.summary: Leaders from Fiji and Vanuatu have urged packaging brands to design for local realities at the COP31 summit. A report from Common Seas calls for the Global Plastics Treaty to set harmonized design rules and fund regional waste systems as climate infrastructure.

stories.title: Adani Energy secures 2,500 MW renewable power deal with WBSEDCL
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions will supply up to 2,500 MW of renewable energy to West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co Ltd. The contract includes a 1,750 MW base supply starting in 2028 and a 750 MW greenshoe option. The power will be delivered round the clock.

stories.title: Verbund places 600 million euro green bond
stories.summary: Utility company Verbund has placed a 600 million euro green bond with an eight-year maturity. The company says the proceeds will support infrastructure investment in grids, renewable generation and storage capacity. The issue reportedly attracted strong institutional demand across several European markets.

stories.title: India building automation market projected to reach 12.56 billion dollars by 2030
stories.summary: The Indian building automation market is expected to grow from 4.32 billion dollars in 2025 to 12.56 billion dollars by 2030. The growth is attributed to artificial intelligence, connected systems and energy optimisation. Industry leaders discussed these projections at ORGATEC India 2026 in Mumbai.

stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions wins 25-year renewable supply contract
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions has secured a 25-year contract to supply renewable energy to West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co Ltd. The deal covers 1,750 MW starting in 2028, with a 750 MW greenshoe option available. The award followed a competitive bidding process.

stories.title: Amazon plans 7 billion dollar renewable energy investment in India
stories.summary: Amazon has announced plans to invest 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030. This initiative is in addition to 4 billion dollars in previously contracted projects. The company says the investment aims to support its growing electricity requirements in the country.

stories.title: Chubu Electric invests 1,350 crore rupees in Continuum Green Energy
stories.summary: Japan's Chubu Electric has invested 1,350 crore rupees in Continuum Green Energy. The deal provides the Indian firm with technical expertise and access to Japanese industrial clients. A nominee from the Japanese utility will join the board of the company founded by two IIM Ahmedabad classmates.

stories.title: Meta reviews 2030 net-zero goal as emissions rise
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero emissions target after reporting a 45 percent increase in net emissions during 2025. The company cited the energy demands of its artificial intelligence buildout. Meta previously spent six years telling investors and regulators it would reach its climate goals.

stories.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net zero target
stories.summary: Meta is reviewing its 2030 net zero emissions commitment as artificial intelligence infrastructure increases energy consumption. Executives noted the company had expected clean energy costs to decline and infrastructure to develop more quickly. The company is now re-evaluating its timelines, priorities and interim targets.

stories.title: Meta emissions rise 45 percent amid AI expansion
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero and water-positive goals as data center energy demands grow. The company's 2026 sustainability report confirms that emissions rose 45 percent last year. Meta says it remains committed to its environmental goals while adjusting its interim milestones.

research.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
research.summary: A remarkable 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia reveals that early humans once thrived beside enormous lakes filled with wildlife in what is now a vast desert. Thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains suggest these prehistoric people used sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially including weapons enhanced with poisonous.
